overall: Okay, real talk. This is way better than I expected from an adult-made quiz. The Uno stack, the limited banner, the family holiday, 'optional' Sunday dinner, the contest song and hiding the video link on slide 10 are genuinely funny and I would send those to my group chat. The problems are the stuff you notice by card 20. One: every feeling card says 'What showed up first?', seven times, and by chapter 4 I'm tapping without reading. Two: the jokes repeat. 'Future me' three times, 'already has a job' or 'has plans' three times, instant noodles twice, 'zero guilt' twice, 'Fair is fair' twice, 'my two favorites' twice in chapter 1, and 'Pick the two that are the most you' is the same prompt in C4-8 and C7-9. That's exactly how you lose someone. Three: about six cards are 'who pays when a friend is broke', which is the repeat-answer thing all over again. Four: a lot of teen versions are still adult versions with a school word swapped in: golf, shared calendars, couches up four flights, five-star course reviews, and three 'someday' cards in the family chapter. Give me the version that's happening to me now: parents away for the weekend, the coach's kid, the easy-A elective, shared locations. Teen-safety is mostly handled (18+ cards gated, 'parents set my phone rules' is smart), but fix two things: the third-night 11:48pm card has to read as drama, not a friend in crisis, and C6-7 can fire a locked18 wedding tag for a minor. Also, nobody my age says 'Be my person?' and 'Chill Personified' is exactly what I mean by adults trying to sound young. Half-names mostly slap: Human Weighted Blanket, Old-School Final Boss, Low-Key Tryhard, Side-Quest Knight. Cut the plant card, it's the one with an obvious good-person answer.
